## CEO BRIEFING

**Incident summary:** At 11:42 UTC, the Batch API began returning elevated 502 errors on a subset of customer accounts. The issue was isolated to one internal worker fleet (fleet-a) and did not affect other API surfaces. We applied a mitigation at 12:58 by moving all Batch API traffic to the healthy fleet (fleet-b). Error rates dropped to near baseline within minutes and are currently at 0.3% (baseline 0.2%). We are in a 90-minute verification window that closes at 14:30 UTC. Root cause is not yet established; we have two hypotheses under investigation (a connection-pool change in today's release and concentrated load). We are re-driving failed jobs for affected accounts (60% complete, no failures on re-drive). No other APIs are impacted.

**Who is hit:** Seven customer accounts experienced failures during the incident window (11:42–12:58). All are on the affected fleet. One of them, Contoso, has an SLA with service credits; we will handle that per contract after month-end determination. The other six are on standard terms.

**What to say on the board call:** We experienced a partial degradation of the Batch API this morning, affecting a small number of customers. We mitigated it quickly and are monitoring recovery. We are investigating the root cause and will provide a full update once the verification window closes. Service is currently stable and error rates are near normal. We have one customer with potential SLA credits, which we will address per our contractual process.

---

## ENGINEERING UPDATE

**Current status (14:20 UTC):** Incident INC-2026-1109-01 is OPEN, mitigated, verification in progress. All Batch API traffic is on fleet-b; fleet-a is drained and out of rotation. Error rate on `POST /v1/batch/jobs` is 0.3% (baseline 0.2%). Verification window closes at 14:30 UTC. Re-drive of failed jobs is ~60% complete with no failures.

**Root cause:** Not established. Two hypotheses remain live, neither tested:
- **H1 (leading):** Connection-pool change in `batch-api@2026.11.09-r3` (max pool size lowered from 80 to 24 per worker). Shipped at 11:31, first page at 11:42. Fleet-a workers observed queueing on DB connections. Against: same release on fleet-b caused no issues.
- **H2:** Concentrated load on fleet-a (~3x morning average from 11:38, driven by wonka-industries). Against: fleet-a handled higher peak on 2026-11-03 without errors.
- H3 (upstream storage provider) rejected at 11:47.

**Next steps:**
1. Continue monitoring until 14:30. If error rate stays ≤0.4% for the full window, we can declare the incident resolved (per policy).
2. After verification, run the rollback test on fleet-a to test H1 (roll back r3 and observe if errors recur under load). This will require coordination with Marcus.
3. Determine whether to return fleet-a to rotation only after root cause is confirmed and fixed.
4. Complete re-drive of failed jobs for all affected accounts.
5. Note: SEC-411 (unrelated to this incident) – batch worker DB role has over-permission to billing schema. Marcus owns it, target this week.

**Action items:** Priya to continue monitoring and report at 14:30. Marcus to prepare rollback test plan. Tomas to handle customer communications. Ruth to publish status page update.

## CUSTOMER EMAIL

**Subject:** Update on Batch API incident – your account impact

Dear Contoso,

We are writing in response to your tickets (TKT-8903 and TKT-8907) regarding the Batch API errors you experienced this morning.

We confirm that your account was affected by an incident that began at 11:42 UTC and was mitigated at 12:58 UTC. During the incident window (11:42–12:58), your account made 9,400 Batch API requests, of which 3,410 returned errors (502). We have applied a mitigation that has restored service, and error rates are now near normal. We are also re-driving the failed jobs for affected accounts; your re-drive is in progress and we will confirm completion.

Regarding your question about service credits under Schedule B: we cannot determine monthly availability until the end of the calendar month, as per the contract. We will publish the availability figure within 10 business days of month end, and you may submit a credit claim within 30 days of that publication. We will provide a formal response on credits at that time.

We will keep you updated on the incident status. If you have any further questions, please reply to this email or contact our support team.

Sincerely,
Northstar Support

---

## STATUS PAGE UPDATE

**Update on Batch API incident – 14:20 UTC**

We are continuing to investigate the elevated error rates on the Batch API that began at 11:42 UTC. A mitigation has been applied and error rates have significantly decreased. We are monitoring the service and re-driving failed jobs for affected customers. We will provide another update by 14:30 UTC.

Other Northstar APIs are unaffected.

*Investigating.*
